Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

brag verb

also boast, show off about, he brags too much about his money, show off, boastful, talk big, bluster, boasting

classical

Caes. BC 3.83: jactāre urbānam grātiam et dignitātem (Lewis & Short)
Cic. de Or. 2.209: intolerantius sē jactāre (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 94, 150
Traupman 157

jactō, jactāre, jactāvī, jactātum

verb, first conjugation, with the thing boasted of in the accusative; sē jactāre, to brag

boast of, brag about

Literally “to keep throwing about”.

Other words

  • jactāns, jactantis — boastful

    declension · also used · classical · Traupman 149; Traupman 281

  • ampullor, ampullārī, ampullātus sum — talk big, use bombast

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Hor. Ep. 1.3.14: tragicā ampullātur in arte (Lewis & Short); Traupman 279

    From ampulla, a round flask: swollen talk. Probably coined by Horace (Lewis & Short).

  • jactātiō, jactātiōnis f. — boasting, showing off

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Lewis & Short; Traupman 281

Examples

  • Pecūniam nimis jactat.

    He brags too much about his money.Traupman 94

SourcesLewis & Short: jacto

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 94.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
